This report today is regarding an application from YWCA Saskatoon to amend the existing zoning agreement for 510 25th Street East.
Now the subject property 510 25th Street East is the current location of the YWCA Saskatoon and the Saskatoon Community Service Village facilities.
This site is located in the city park neighborhood adjacent to Kinzman Park here as well as downtown just to the south.
The site is currently zoned M3 General Institutional District and is subject to a zoning agreement.

As a quick reminder, a zoning agreement is a regulatory tool that is used to control development of a specific piece of property through a legal agreement that is tied to and runs with the land and ensures that only a specific development proposal and specific land uses, although can be constructed and occur on the property.

Now the existing zoning agreement for this site currently provides for the wide range of uses on the property that reflect the programs and services currently offered within the YWCA and service village facilities.
Here's a proposed site plan of the site with the existing complex as well as the proposal that's the subject of this application.

The YWCA has submitted this application proposing to constructed building addition that would contain 18 dwelling units to be operated by the YWCA and include support services for residents of those units.

The addition is proposed in this location as two floors constructed above the existing parking lot on the seat side of the property and the design is proposed would allow for that existing parking surface at very level to be maintained.

These amendments are outlined in the appendix four of the report and primarily includes adding dwelling units as a permitted use on the property as well as other more minor adjustments to the sites development standards to allow for the construction of the addition in the location proposed.

Public engagement undertaken with respect to this application included mail notification to 378 property owners located within approximately 150 meters at the site as well as to the word counselor for the area and the city park community association.
The application was also placed on the engage page of the city's website.
The date from our engagement we have received correspondence from just one area resident to express support for the proposal.
This application was also reviewed by other civic departments as part of our standard administrative review process and no concerns were identified from that review.
The proposal is in conformance with relevant sections of the official community plan and other requirements of the city.
And therefore administration is recommending that this rezoning application to amend the existing agreement for this site be approved.
